title: Solar Panels and Photovoltaics
text: Solar panels convert sunlight into electricity through the photovoltaic effect, in which photons strike semiconductor material (typically silicon) and excite electrons into a higher energy state, generating an electric current. A solar cell is the basic unit; multiple cells form panels, which are combined into arrays. Solar panel efficiency has improved dramatically, from about 6% in the 1950s to over 26% for commercial panels today. The cost of solar electricity has fallen by over 90% since 2010, making it the cheapest electricity source in history in most parts of the world. Global installed solar capacity has grown from less than 10 GW in 2007 to over 1 terawatt by 2022.
